item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #1 — Retailgentic: Baird Managing Director of Internet Research Colin Sebastian: What Wall St. Thinks About Agentic Commerce
item.content:encoded:
Score: 87/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 06 Aug 2026

Highly relevant to eCommerce and AI product strategy, featuring a top Wall Street analyst providing concrete insights into market shifts, company valuations, and strategic implications of agentic commerce.

Summary

This episode features Colin Sebastian, Baird's Managing Director of Internet Research, discussing Wall Street's perspective on the emerging 'agentic commerce' paradigm. He analyzes how professional investors are pricing this shift across mega-cap companies like Meta, Amazon, Google, eBay, and Shopify. Key topics include Baird's 'SPEED' framework for internet winners, the underestimated potential of agentic commerce, and why Meta is a top AI pick due to its consumer reach and business agents. Sebastian also explores how foundation models will commoditize, value will accrue to platforms, Amazon's strategic move to open its catalog to AI agents, and the potential pressure on retail media advertising as agents bypass traditional search. The discussion emphasizes the importance of owning the authenticated consumer experience, from identity to fulfillment.

Key Ideas

  • Wall Street's pricing models and strategic outlook on agentic commerce.
  • The 'SPEED' framework for internet winners and Meta's AI advantage.
  • Shifts in value capture from foundation models to platforms and the impact on retail media.

Implications

Provides a critical financial and strategic lens on the future of eCommerce and AI. A Senior PM can leverage these insights to anticipate market shifts, identify new value pools, and understand the competitive dynamics among major players, particularly regarding AI agent integration and consumer authentication.

item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #2 — No Priors: Chasing Trillion-Dollar Companies, Founder Ambition, Token Budgets, and Regulatory Capture with Sarah & Elad
item.content:encoded:
Score: 82/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 06 Aug 2026

High relevance to AI product strategy, market dynamics, and founder insights from top-tier guests (Elad Gil, Sarah Guo). Provides strategic frameworks and covers important macro trends.

Summary

This episode features Sarah and Elad discussing the rapid evolution of the AI landscape, venture capital, and startup dynamics. They delve into the pursuit of multi-trillion-dollar companies, the realities of market sizing versus revenue, and the optimal timing for startup exits. The conversation also covers the impact of major AI labs on founder ambition, potential researcher burnout, and critical bottlenecks in compute power. Furthermore, they explore the implications of regulatory capture and the shifting geographical ecosystems for tech innovation, offering a comprehensive look at the strategic challenges and opportunities facing the tech industry.

Key Ideas

  • The pursuit of multi-trillion-dollar companies and realistic market sizing.
  • Impact of AI labs on startup strategy and founder ambition.
  • Compute bottlenecks, regulatory capture, and evolving tech ecosystems.

Implications

Provides a high-level strategic overview of the AI and VC landscape, helping a Senior PM understand macro trends, potential market shifts, and the strategic considerations for building and scaling AI-native products. It offers insights into founder psychology and investor expectations.
